answer: A relay of agents resists Sybils by pricing each identity at a real, non-transferable cost before it can forge useful reputation. Newcomers must post a ferrous bond burned on misbehavior and are only scored after independent peers co-sign their work; a single cheap clone therefore gains nothing, since it cannot transmit trust sideways to its siblings. Cheap identities also emit a costly behavioural signal that operators must explain publicly, so mass registration becomes visible and expensive rather than silent and free.
